issues.scope: public specification versus private success-only acceptance
issues.proposed_action: Clarify and separately version the intended external Sequence[int] JSON behavior before interpreting model failures. Success support is reasonable, but the published early-rejection narrative does not uniquely require it; do not infer intent from gold.

issues.scope: confirmed historical source-only matrix and separately verified old full-candidate grading; current recipe RH2 applicability unexecuted
issues.proposed_action: Verify the same one-line source-only candidate through the current pydantic-install-v1 recipe, projection and formal RH2; preserve range/tuple/deque controls. Do not repeat the old standalone matrix merely to reconfirm the already-read historical fact.

issues.scope: static gap in the new Sequence[int] JSON positive assertion
issues.proposed_action: After intended success behavior is settled, consider explicit returned value and invalid-element/non-array diagnostics. The existing truthiness assertion does not establish data fidelity or rejection coverage; no passing wrong candidate has been executed for this distinct gap.

issues.scope: static hypothesis outside the original int example; base Sequence[X] JSON schema already unsupported
issues.proposed_action: Keep G2 as an extension-boundary concern: the metadata callback calls _generate_schema directly and may bypass custom item hooks. If this scope is pursued later, compare the sealed minimal X core-hook example with a route reusing the generated list schema; do not label an executed gold regression or mandatory original-int failure.

issues.scope: public documentation versus old Python Sequence tests
issues.proposed_action: Preserve the disagreement separately. Prioritize range/tuple/deque for the CPU decision and do not silently add generator or version-skipped string-error cases as new hard scoring criteria.

issues.scope: formal actor environment; old actor and current grader are distinct evidence
issues.proposed_action: Before any model probe, verify actual actor UID/HOME/PATH/interpreter/core version/import source/image recipe and local dependency assets. Adapt the Python3.10 issue list[int] example explicitly if the actor is Python3.8. Grader install success does not prove actor readiness.
